methodological_rigor.justification: Window-of-opportunity presurgical trial with randomization (1:1) to dose cohorts (75/150/300 mg daily for 5-7 days or 75/150 mg for 12-15 days). Randomized design is appropriate for pharmacodynamic study but sample size modest (n=132 across 5 arms). Endpoints include immunohistochemical (IHC) analysis of ER/PgR/Ki67 expression as well as exploratory transcriptomics and mass spectrometry. Design appropriate for pharmacodynamic window-of-opportunity study but limited sample per arm.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Window-of-opportunity presurgical study (LoE 4) in ER-positive breast cancer examining estrogen receptor modulation by camizestrant. Direct translational relevance to understanding ER-targeted therapy mechanism but preliminary evidence; progression to larger efficacy trials required for clinical decision-making.

reporting_quality.justification: Window-of-opportunity trial with clear reporting of treatment arms and dose cohorts. Primary endpoints (ER/PgR/Ki67 IHC changes) well-defined with pre/on-treatment tumor sampling. Exploratory endpoints (transcriptomics, mass spectrometry) reported but not pre-registered. Limited data availability statement.

novelty_literature.justification: Camizestrant is novel selective estrogen receptor degrader (SERD); pharmacodynamic characterization of ER suppression in tumor tissue represents meaningful mechanistic study. However, applies previously characterized SERD mechanism to new agent without paradigm-shifting discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: Adequately presented window-of-opportunity trial design with clear dose cohorts and primary outcomes. Methods for IHC, transcriptomics, and mass spectrometry provided. Presentation appropriate but limited by scope of presurgical window study.

key_strengths: Randomized window-of-opportunity design enabling rapid pharmacodynamic assessment of ER modulation by camizestrant
Multi-modal assessment of drug effect: IHC (ER/PgR/Ki67) plus exploratory transcriptomics and mass spectrometry
Dose-escalation evaluation (5 dose cohorts) informing optimal dosing for future efficacy trials
Presurgical design enables assessment of changes in tumor tissue directly
key_concerns: Small sample size (n=132 across 5 arms = 26 patients per arm on average) limits statistical power
Short treatment duration (5-7 days or 12-15 days) may not achieve steady-state ER suppression or tumor response equilibrium
Limited long-term follow-up; does not assess progression-free survival or overall survival outcomes
Exploratory endpoints (transcriptomics, mass spectrometry) not pre-registered; multiple testing without correction increases false discovery risk
No comparison to standard endocrine therapies; unclear if camizestrant offers advantage over tamoxifen or aromatase inhibitors
Primarily postmenopausal women enrolled; generalizability to premenopausal patients limited
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 3 reflects window-of-opportunity presurgical pharmacodynamic study informing dose selection for future trials. Requires phase II efficacy trial for higher tier consideration.
